messages.author: 49e229eeadc99c45
messages.subject: Rsubread missing paired sequences
parts:
Hello,

I'm using Rsubread to align MiSeq paired-end sequences to hg18 and I have a question about how sequence 'pairs' are identified.  

The pipeline I'm developing uses the command align(index=indexPath, readfile1="p2.fa", readfile2="p1.fa", output_file=paste0(runName,".bam"), nthreads=8, nBestLocations=10, minFragLength=0, maxFragLength=1200, output_format="BAM").  Rsubread outputs that it processed 148273 fragments, mapped 146107 fragments (98.5%) and 'correctly paired' 83812 fragments.  When I read the corresponding BAM file using readGAlignmentsFromBam with scanBamFlags set to isUnmappedQuery=FALSE, isPaired=TRUE, hasUnmappedMate=FALSE, and isProperPair=TRUE, and do some filtering for alignment quality, I see roughly the expected number of pairs as reported by Rsubread (I see 63331 out of 83812, it's very feasible that my alignment quality filtering would remove that many sequences).  However, if I change the scanBamFlags to  only isUnmappedQuery=FALSE and pair-up the sequences myself (splitting by read name, removing alignments with <95% sequence identity, removing reads without one + and one - strand hit, and then using reduce(x, min.gapwidth=1200)), I see significantly more 'pairs' of sequences (119366 to be exact).

All of these manually-curated 'pairs' should have the same characteristics that Rsubread is looking for during pair-picking (presuming I'm understanding what's going on 'under the hood').  My manual pairs consist of two alignments, one from each end of the same cluster, one aligning to each strand of the genome, and the sequences cannot be more than 1200bp apart (a reasonable number given our bead purification scheme, this is also the number I provided to Rsubread for maxFragLength).  Furthermore, I hand-picked a few of the manually-curated pairs that were not marked by Rsubread and BLATed the sequences and saw perfect 100% matches that agreed with the alignments provided by Rsubread.

Am I not asking Rsubread to pair sequences in the right way or is there a reason that Rsubread seems to be miss marking some pairs of sequences as 'paired'?  If it's of any help/interest, I've noticed that Rsubread does a far better job at finding pairs in sets of reads with low alignment diversity.  Some of our samples consist solely of reads that map to one location in the genome and Rsubread pairs those reads far more effectively than for samples where reads represent many different genomic coordinates.  I capture roughly 5% more pairs by manually curating low-diversity samples but up to 300% more pairs in high-diversity regions.

Let me know if you'd like a few sample sequences (maybe one that is marked as paired and one that is only caught by manual curation?) 

Thanks!

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Rsubread missing paired sequences
parts:
Dear Eric,

Could you firstly let me know the version of Rsubread you are using and the type of your data (RNA-seq or DNA-seq)?

The situation you described seems to be quite complex because you output multi-mapping reads (nBestLocations=10) and also you performed filtering.

I think there are possibly two reasons why you got more pairs of reads. The first is that the min.gapwidth parameter in reduce function seems to specify the gap size between the two reads from the same pair, whereas the maxFragLength parameter in align function specifies the length of the sequencing fragment/template. When their values are the same, the reduce function actually allows bigger fragment size and thus gives you more paired reads.

The other reason is that I am afraid the order of multi-mapping reads might be changed after your processing and this could give you incorrect read pairing. For example, read removal may result in a read being paired with itself from an alternative mapping. This may explain why you got a lot more pairs in high-diversity regions. You may check if the reads from the extra pairs you got are in different positions of the fragment (one should be the first segment and the other should be the second segment).

Hope this helps.


Best regards,
Wei

messages.author: 49e229eeadc99c45
messages.subject: Re: Rsubread missing paired sequences
parts:
Hi Wei,

Thanks for the fast reply!

I'm using Rsubread version 1.12.3 and R version 3.0.1.  The data is from DNA.  Briefly, I’m using a PCR-based approach to make amplicons around viral integration sites in human genomic DNA.

Good idea about the differences between min.gapwidth and maxFragLength - I reduced min.gapwidth such that it will always return fewer reads than maxFragLength.  This slightly reduced the number of additional sites that manual curating discovered, however I'm still seeing more pairs than are identified by Rsubread.

The additional pairs that I'm seeing are often from megabases away (if not different chromosomes completely) from the ones identified by Rsubread, so I don't think that reads being paired with an alternative mapping is the issue.  Just to double-check, I added the conditions that each manually curated pair may only contain two reads, each read must be from a different strand (as true paired-end reads should be), and that one read must have isFirstMateRead=TRUE and the other read must have isSecondMateRead=TRUE (it's my understanding that these refer to the files provided for readfile1 and readfile2 respectively).  Unfortunately I'm still seeing the extra pairs show up.  Another observation I noticed while implementing these checks is that even when I ask for every result in the entire alignment (res = scanBam(fileName, index=indexName, param=ScanBamParam(what=c('qname')))), every result is only repeated twice.  When I ask for results with isFirstMateRead=TRUE or isSecondMateRead=TRUE, I never see the same name twice.  Is this normal behavior given that the alignment was performed with nBestLocations=10?

I also did a test where I changed the settings to isUnmappedQuery=FALSE, isPaired=TRUE, hasUnmappedMate=FALSE (different from my first test where I also included isProperPair=TRUE).  This time, my results very closely match what I see when I ask for all reads where isUnmappedQuery=FALSE, suggesting that the isProperPair=TRUE flag is what limited the pairs I previously observed.  Interestingly, the number of unique read names observed with  isProperPair=TRUE is exactly equal to the number of pairs reported by Rsubread in the R console after the align command.  I can’t find any information in the SAM/BAM file specifications regarding exactly what constitutes a ‘proper pair’ – it seems that this designation is up to the aligner’s discretion.  Can you shed some light on the criteria Rsubread uses to mark ‘proper pairs’?  I think the phenomenon must just be a difference in my criteria vs. Rsubread’s criteria for what makes a ‘proper’ pair. 

Thanks so much for your help!

- Eric

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Rsubread missing paired sequences
parts:
Hi Eric,

The criteria for calling a proper pair in Rsubread include the following:
(1) The two reads from the same pair must both be mapped.
(2) They have to be mapped to different stands (one on positive strand and the other on negative strand).
(3) The fragment length derived from the mapping results of the two reads must be within the specified range [minFragLength, maxFragLength].

I would suggest you to ask in the bioconductor mailing list about the criteria used in readGAlignmentsFromBam and scanBam. I'm not sure what the criteria they use.

Best regards,
Wei
